_comment: The patcher window's "?" guides. One short, plain guide for every public patch (by patch id), every population mode (by mode id) and every button, tool and setting (by control key). Each guide is a list of short lines: what it does, how to use it, and what to watch out for. tests/test_how_to_use.py refuses a public patch, mode or control without one, and a guide that is too long or uses technical words. Write each from what the feature really does (its description in the patcher, README and How to Use.txt).

guide: Every time a villager practises Farming, Building, Research, Healing or Parenting at work, the skill check succeeds, so skills grow faster.
Nothing to click: tick it, patch, and play as usual.
How much a success adds, and everything else about the job, stays the game's own.
Off in Default Patches and Owner's Defaults: tick it yourself if you want it.

Nothing extra to click: run the lessons as you normally do.
Want lessons to stop at 50? Also tick Teaching Children Stops at 50.
A villager who finishes Recovering at the hospital gains 1 health point (up to 100).
Nothing to click: it happens whenever a hospital recovery ends.
In the original game, recovering at the hospital does not change health at all.

stock: Keeps each game's normal population limit: A New Home 90, The Lost Children 115, The Secret City 125, The Tree of Life 115, New Believers 105.
Pick this to play with the original game's limits.
Twins, triplets and island events still never overfill the villager places.
collection_progression: Collections keep raising the population limit as you complete them.
A New Home and The Lost Children can reach 256; the other three reach 150 (256 with 256 Villagers).
Pick this if you like to earn a bigger village.
immediate_fixed: The highest population limit is open straight away: 256 in A New Home and The Lost Children, 150 in the other three (256 with 256 Villagers).
Collections no longer change the limit.
Pick this for the biggest village from the start.

select_all.title: Select All Patches
guide: Ticks every patch for every game.
Except 256 Villagers (Experimental), which you tick yourself.
It does not change the population mode.

default_patches.title: Default Patches
guide: Ticks the recommended set: every patch except Learning Skills Never Fails, Manual Drop-Breeding, Story / Cheat Upgrades and 256 Villagers,
and except the two cheats: VV1 Mushroom/Collectible Duplication Cheat and Super-Secret Golden Mushroom.
This is what a fresh install starts with.
It does not change the population mode.

owners_defaults.title: Owner's Defaults
guide: Ticks the patcher owner's own choice: every patch except Learning Skills Never Fails.
That includes Story / Cheat Upgrades and 256 Villagers (Experimental), which uses its own save folder.
It does not change the population mode.

deselect_all.title: Deselect All Patches
guide: Unticks every patch, so you can tick just the ones you want.
The population mode you chose still applies.

output_location.title: Modded output location
guide: Click Choose Folder... to pick where the modded copies go.
Each game is made inside it as "(Game name) - Modded".
Leave it blank to put each copy beside its original game folder.

choose_exe.title: Original game executable
guide: Click Browse... and choose the original game's .exe, as downloaded from Last Day of Work.
The blue line below says which game it found.
The original game is never changed.

validate.title: Validate
guide: Checks that the chosen game is a supported original, and shows the population limit of the mode you picked.
Nothing is written.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
guide: A practice run: checks the game and prepares every ticked patch, but writes no files.
Shows where the modded copy would be made.

create_modified_exe.title: Create Modified EXE
guide: 1. Pick a population mode and tick the patches you want.
2. Browse to the original game's .exe, then click Create Modified EXE.
A complete copy named "(Game name) - Modded" is made with the modded game in it; the original is never changed.
The patcher's own files go in a "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files" folder inside the copy.
Play the .exe in the copy. Its saves go in their own "- Modded" folder in Documents\LDW.
Patching again replaces the copy (it asks first); your saves are not touched.

game_folders.title: Game folders
guide: Choose one folder per game, each holding that game's original .exe.
Use Choose Folder... on a row, or Find All 5 in Parent Folder... to fill them all.
The original folders are never changed.

find_all_5.title: Find All 5 in Parent Folder
guide: Choose one folder that holds your five games.
The patcher finds each game's .exe in that folder or one folder below, and fills in the rows.

validate_all_5.title: Validate All 5
guide: Checks that all five chosen games are supported originals.
Nothing is written.

dry_run_all_5.title: Dry Run All 5
guide: A practice run for all five games: checks them and prepares every ticked patch, but writes no files.

patch_all_5.title: Patch All 5
guide: 1. Pick a population mode and tick the patches you want.
2. Fill in all five game folders, then click Patch All 5.
Each game gets a complete copy named "(Game name) - Modded"; the originals are never changed.
The patcher's own files go in a "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files" folder inside each copy.
Copying five games can take several minutes.

open_vanilla_folder.title: Open Vanilla Folder
guide: Opens the original game's folder in File Explorer.

open_modified_folder.title: Open Modified Folder
guide: Opens the modded copy's folder in File Explorer, where the modded game's .exe is.
Patch the game first.

open_game_folder.title: Open Game Folder
guide: After patching, opens the new modded folder in File Explorer.

back_up_saves.title: Back Up Saves
guide: Copies a game's save folders (your saves and the patcher's logs) into a dated Backups folder inside each one.
Click Back Up Saves, tick the save folders you want, then Back Up Selected.
The game can stay open: it is paused for the copy, but the backup holds the village as of its last save.
Old backups are never replaced or deleted.

restore_saves.title: Restore Saves
guide: Puts a backup back: the whole save folder, or one save slot.
Quit the game first, from its own menu.
Choose a backup, choose whole folder or one slot, then Restore...; you are shown what will change first.
Your saves as they are now are backed up first, so a restore can be undone.
Delete Backup... removes a backup you no longer want (it asks first).

rename_tribe.title: Rename Tribe
guide: Changes a tribe's name inside its save.
Quit the game first, from its own menu.
Pick the game, save folder and tribe, type the new name and click Rename.
The save folder is backed up first, so you can undo it with Restore Saves.
The patcher's logs carry on for the same village under the new name.

check_logs.title: Check Logs
guide: Checks whether the patcher's logs and data files for a village agree with its save.
That includes masks still kept for villagers who are no longer in the village.
Pick the game, save folder and tribe, then click Check.
Each file is marked OK, WRONG, NOTE or UNCHECKED.
It only reads, so the game may stay open.

repair_logs.title: Repair Logs
guide: Your go-ahead for the game to fix a village's logs.
Quit the game first, then pick the game, save folder and tribe; the logs are checked and the result shown.
Confirm: the save folder is backed up first.
Then play that tribe and quit the game from its menu: everything found wrong is repaired, without asking.
Masks kept for villagers who are no longer in the village are removed too.

check_logs_automatically.title: Check logs automatically
guide: On by default. Games you create while it is ticked check each village's logs quietly while you play.
Only if something is wrong, you are asked Repair or Not now when you close the game, never during play.
Repair fixes it (backed up first); Not now changes nothing and asks again next time.
To turn it off, untick this box and patch the game again; a game already made keeps its own setting.

check_for_updates.title: Check for updates
guide: Opens the patcher's GitHub page, where the newest version is listed.
Your version is shown just above the link.
